cards.text: Proverbs is a book of wise sayings, and here a father is talking to his sons. Listen, he says, pay attention and gain understanding, because I give you sound teaching. I say LISTEN UP to an empty bakery every morning, friend, and the oven still hasn't interrupted me once.

cards.question: The father says his teaching is sound. So what does he tell his sons not to do with his directive?

cards.text: Then the father thinks back to when he was a boy, tender and the only child of his mother. Only child. Nobody else to blame for the crumbs.

cards.question: The father is about to pass along what his own father taught him.

cards.text: Now Grandpa's talking: "Let your heart lay hold of my words; keep my commands and you will live." A hand-me-down speech, passed down like a cookie recipe NOBODY is allowed to change.

cards.question: Grandpa tells his son to get wisdom and get understanding. What does he say not to do with his words?

answers.text: Forget them or turn from them
Change them or add to them

cards.text: Then Grandpa starts talking about wisdom like she's a person. Don't forsake wisdom, he says, and she will preserve you.

cards.question: Love wisdom, says Grandpa, and she will ___ you.

cards.text: Grandpa says it plain: "Wisdom is supreme; so acquire wisdom." Not pretty good, friend, not top five, SUPREME.

cards.question: Grandpa says that whatever else you may get, you should gain understanding.

cards.text: Grandpa keeps going: "Prize her, and she will exalt you; if you embrace her, she will honor you." You hold on to wisdom and SHE lifts YOU up, friend. Best deal I ever heard.

cards.question: Grandpa says wisdom honors whoever embraces her. What does he say she'll present them with?

cards.text: Grandpa's done, and now the father turns back to his own son. Listen, my son, he says, and receive my words.

cards.question: If the son listens and receives his father's words, what does the father promise him?
The father says he'll guide his son in the way of wisdom and lead him on ___ paths.
The father says that on the paths of wisdom, his son might still stumble when he runs.

cards.text: Then he says hold on to instruction, and don't let go. Picture me with the LAST cookie on the tray, friend: NOBODY is prying that loose.

cards.question: The father tells his son to guard instruction. Why?

cards.text: Now the father points to a different road: the path of the wicked, the way of evildoers.

cards.question: The father says it's fine to walk the path of the wicked for a little while, as long as his son doesn't stay on it.

cards.text: Then he tells why: these people cannot sleep unless they do evil. I lost sleep in that junk drawer worrying, friend, but these folks lose sleep because they HAVEN'T done anything wrong yet.

cards.question: The wicked are deprived of slumber until they make someone ___.

cards.text: And what's on their table? They eat the bread of wickedness and drink the wine of violence.
Now the father paints two pictures. The path of the righteous is like the first gleam of dawn.

cards.question: The path of the righteous is like the first gleam of dawn. What happens to that light?

answers.text: It flickers and then goes out

cards.question: The way of the wicked is like the darkest gloom, and they know exactly what makes them stumble.

cards.text: Then the father comes back to his son: pay attention to my words, and incline your ear to my sayings. That's leaning IN, friend, like a whole room when somebody says "okay, don't tell anybody, but..."

cards.question: The father tells his son not to lose sight of his words. Where should his son keep them?
The father's words are life to those who find them, and health to the whole ___.

cards.text: Then comes the big one: guard your heart with all diligence. That's how I guard my chocolate chips, friend, and if anybody else lived up here, they'd tell you.

cards.question: Why does the father say to guard your heart with all diligence?

answers.text: Springs of life flow from it
Others will try to steal it

cards.text: From the heart, the father moves to the mouth: put away deception, and keep your lips from perverse speech.

cards.question: After the mouth, the father turns to the eyes. He says to keep them looking around for danger on every side.

cards.text: Then the feet: make a level path for your feet, and all your ways will be sure. Heart, mouth, eyes, feet. He's packing the WHOLE person into this box, friend.

cards.question: The father wants a level path and eyes fixed straight ahead. So what does he say about swerving?

findings.problem: The joke compares Grandpa's speech to 'a cookie recipe NOBODY is allowed to change.' The next card asks what Grandpa says not to do with his words, and one of its wrong answers is 'Change them or add to them.' The setup points the baker toward a wrong answer instead of helping them reason to the right one (Proverbs 4:5 says do not forget them or turn from them).

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The blank is the last word of the line in Proverbs 4:16 ('until they make someone ___'). 'fall' and 'pay' are equally reasonable from what the baker has seen, so the card tests wording, not meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The blank is the last word of the line in Proverbs 4:22 ('health to the whole ___'). Nothing earlier lets the baker reason between 'body,' 'household' and 'nation,' so it is a guess at the wording.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'Swerve only to avoid trouble' can be argued as right. The same verse says 'turn your feet away from evil' (Proverbs 4:27), and Proverbs 4:15 says 'Avoid it… Turn from it and pass on by.'

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The passage's closing instruction, 'turn your feet away from evil' (Proverbs 4:27), is never told on a story card or asked on a choice card. The walkthrough ends without it.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
